explain.say: If you walked from the North Pole to the Equator, the weather around you would change again and again. A scientist called Wladimir Köppen sorted the world’s climates into five big groups, using temperature and rain. Look at the board: they stack from the pole down to the Equator.

explain.say: At the top is group E, polar, where even the warmest month stays below 10 degrees, as in Antarctica and northern Greenland. Brilliant work! Wow fact: mountains break the pattern, so near the Equator you can climb Mount Kilimanjaro from warm farmland to glaciers.

faq.q: What is the Köppen climate classification?
faq.a: It is a way of sorting the world’s climates into five main groups, A to E, by temperature and rainfall. Wladimir Köppen first published it in 1884 and kept improving it, later with Rudolf Geiger.
asks: What are the five Köppen climate groups?

faq.a: In Köppen’s group A, every month averages at least 18 °C. Rainforests get rain all year, while savanna and monsoon places have wet and dry seasons.
asks: Why is it hot all year in the tropics?

faq.q: Why are dry climates found near 30 degrees?
faq.a: Warm air rises at the Equator, flows away and sinks again near 30 degrees north and south. Sinking air warms and dries out, so clouds rarely form, which is why the Sahara, Arabian and Kalahari deserts lie there.
asks: Why are many deserts at the same latitude?
Why are dry climates near 30 degrees?

faq.a: A temperate climate, Köppen’s group C, is mild, without very hot or very cold months. Many temperate places, like London and Buenos Aires, have four clear seasons.

faq.q: What is the polar climate like?
faq.a: In Köppen’s group E, even the warmest month averages below 10 °C. Tundra has mosses, low shrubs and frozen ground called permafrost; ice caps are covered in ice all year.

facts: Köppen's classification has five main groups: A tropical, B dry, C temperate, D continental and E polar.
In Köppen's system a tropical climate has every month averaging at least 18 °C.

quiz.say: In Köppen's system, every month is warmer than 18 °C. Which group is it?
quiz.why: Group A, tropical, has every month averaging at least 18 °C.

wrong.1: Temperate places have cooler months below 18 °C.
wrong.2: In polar places even the warmest month is below 10 °C.

quiz.say: Why are many deserts found near 30 degrees north and south?
quiz.show: Many deserts lie near 30 degrees because…

options.show: Dry air sinks there, so clouds rarely form
options.say: Dry air sinks there, so clouds rarely form

options.show: They are closest to the sun
options.say: They are closest to the sun

quiz.why: Air that rose at the Equator sinks near 30 degrees, warming and drying so that rain clouds cannot grow.

wrong.1: All places on Earth are about the same distance from the sun.
wrong.2: Warm oceans add moisture; deserts form where air is dry.
